cards.explanation: The answer is False. The singer says, "My soul longs, even faints, for the courts of the LORD; my heart and my flesh cry out for the living God." (Psalm 84:2). Nobody who faints from wanting something says "no rush." This man's whole self is calling out.

The answer is her young. The swallow found a nest "…where she places her young near Your altars…" (Psalm 84:3). A mama bird picked her spot, and she picked it right next to the altars. I think she knew what she was doing, friends.

The answer is True. The singer says, "How blessed are those who dwell in Your house! They are ever praising You." (Psalm 84:4). Ever praising means it doesn't stop. I wish my mixer had that kind of commitment, friends.

The answer is in the LORD. The singer says, "Blessed are those whose strength is in You, whose hearts are set on pilgrimage." (Psalm 84:5) The "You" is the LORD, so that's where their strength is. Their strength isn't packed in their bags. It's in the LORD, and that's a good thing to carry on a long road, friends.

The answer is springs. "As they pass through the Valley of Baca, they make it a place of springs…" (Psalm 84:6). Springs, as in water. The travelers walk through, and the valley comes out of it different. That's a good walk, friends.

The answer is False. The singer says, "They go from strength to strength, until each appears before God in Zion." (Psalm 84:7) They don't turn back. Each one makes it to Zion and appears before God. No U-turns on this road, friends.

The answer is God's anointed. "Take notice of our shield, O God, and look with favor on the face of Your anointed." (Psalm 84:9). The singer asks God to look with favor on the face of His anointed. The song doesn't say here who that is, so I'll leave it right there, friends.

The answer is better than a thousand elsewhere. The singer says, "For better is one day in Your courts than a thousand elsewhere." (Psalm 84:10) One day against a thousand, and the one day wins. That's some math I can get behind, friends!

The answer is False. The singer says, "I would rather be a doorkeeper in the house of my God than dwell in the tents of the wicked." (Psalm 84:10). A doorkeeper is the one at the entrance of God's house. That's the place he says he would rather be, friends.

The answer is those who walk with integrity. "He withholds no good thing from those who walk with integrity." (Psalm 84:11). The same verse says the LORD God is a sun and a shield, and that He gives grace and glory. That's quite a list, friends.

The answer is the man who trusts in the LORD. The song ends, "O LORD of Hosts, how blessed is the man who trusts in You!" (Psalm 84:12). After all that longing and walking, the last word is about trust. It's a good place to land, friends.
